title: Immuno-localization of definitive hematopoietic stem cells in the vascular niche of mouse fetal liver
protocol: Sacrifice a pregnant mouse 14.5 days post coitus by cervical dislocation.
Wipe the abdomen of the mouse with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Make an incision along the midline with fine scissors.
Continue cutting through the skin on either side of the incision to procure a C-shaped opening perpendicular to the midline of the mouse.
Hold with Graefe forceps and make additional cuts in the peritoneum to expose the abdominal cavity.
Visualize and isolate the uterine horns.
Hold the uterus with Graefe forceps.
Make cuts on the distal ends and the center to excise the uterus completely.
Transfer the uterine horns to a 50 mL sterile polypropylene centrifuge tube containing ice-cold 1× PBS.
Place the uterine horns in a 100 mm cell culture dish containing ice-cold 1× PBS.
Gently remove the endometrial tissue around each conceptus using extra-fine Graefe forceps and Dumont #5 straight forceps.
Transfer the conceptus to a fresh 60 mm cell culture dish with ice-cold 1× PBS using Dumont #5/45 bent-tip forceps.
Use Dumont #5 straight forceps to gently tease away the YS from the fetus.
Be careful not to nick any major blood vessels present in the YS.
Nip the EEVs connecting the fetus to the placenta.
Transfer the fetus to a new 60 mm cell culture dish with minimal ice-cold 1× PBS.
Ensure the fetus remains securely in place during dissection.
Use extra fine Graefe forceps and Dumont #5 straight forceps to tease away fetal tissues from the rostral and caudal ends.
Expose the FL within the abdominal cavity.
Take utmost care not to damage the FL tissue while teasing away surrounding abdominal tissues.
Maintain harvested tissues on ice to reduce lysozyme activity.
Transfer FL tissues isolated into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 1.5 mL ice-cold 4% PFA using Dumont #5/45 bent-tip forceps.
Place the 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes horizontally on ice and put them on a 2D rocker at 30 rpm for 1 hour of fixation.
Remove PFA solution completely after 1 hour.
Add 1.5 mL 1× PBS and give a quick rinse.
Discard the first 1.5 mL of 1× PBS immediately.
Add another 1.5 mL 1× PBS and wash tissues for 30 minutes on ice, horizontally placed on a 2D rocker.
Remove fixative after one hour to prevent over-fixation.
Aspirate buffer from the diametrically opposite side of the tissue during buffer changes.
Discard previous wash buffer before adding fresh buffer each time.
Store E14.5 FLs in fresh 1× PBS at 4°C for up to two months if needed.
Remove 1× PBS and add 1.5 mL 30% sucrose solution.
Place the tube on a tube revolver at 24°C–26°C for 30 minutes for cryo-protection.
Transfer the tubes containing solutions to 4°C for overnight cryo-protection after 30 minutes.
Set up the cryo-mold preparation apparatus as described.
Fill a disposable mold (15 × 15 × 5 mm) with approximately 1.5 mL of PolyFreezeTM cryo-matrix and set it aside.
Crush some dry ice using a mortar and pestle.
Place a stainless steel mold (24 × 24 × 10 mm), containing approximately 2 mL inert 2-methyl butane, on the crushed dry ice.
Place the steel mold on dry ice.
Immerse the tissue in PolyFreezeTM when the 2-methyl butane is cooled for 30-45 seconds.
Gently place the mold containing the floating FL on top of the cold 2-methyl butane using forceps.
Transfer the molds to −80°C after the entire cryo-matrix has solidified.
Keep the mold containing the cryo-block inside the cryotome for at least 30 min before taking cryo-sections.
Maintain the cryotome temperature at -28°C.
Prepare the paraphernalia required for taking cryo-sections and maintain them at -28°C inside the cryotome.
Take a 24-well cell-culture plate and wrap the lid and bottom half separately with aluminum foil.
Label the wells where immunohistochemistry experiments will be carried out.
Fill these labeled wells with 1.5 mL of 1× PBS.
Allow the temperature of the cryo-block to balance with the cryotome for approximately 30 minutes.
Gently press underneath the mold to detach the cryo-block from the mold.
Use cold Graefe forceps to hold the cryo-block, avoiding direct contact with hands.
Pour approximately 1 mL PolyFreezeTM onto a chuck kept at 24°C–26°C.
Place the chuck inside the cryotome and quickly place the cryo-block on the PolyFreeze blob, sticking it to the chuck before the cryo-matrix solidifies.
Press the cryo-block down gently on the chuck using horizontally placed Graefe forceps.
Insert the chuck in the chuck holder after the cryo-matrix has solidified completely (∼2 min).
Tighten the screws on the chuck holder to secure the sample position.
Set the trimming thickness on the cryotome at 50 μm.
Place the cryotome blade in the blade-holding slot and tighten the screws.
Rotate the cryotome wheel handle clockwise to start obtaining sections.
Maintain a steady and continuous movement of the cryotome wheel.
Use separate blades for trimming and sectioning.
Use an older blade for trimming.
Use a newer blade for sectioning to ensure it is free of dents.
Switch to sectioning mode when the sample becomes visible through thinner layers of cryo-matrix.
Set the sectioning thickness at 50 μm.
Change the trimming blade to the sectioning blade.
Rotate the cryotome wheel handle slowly and steadily.
Use a fine brush to pull out single cryo-sections from the edge of the cryotome blade.
Avoid putting the brush bristle on the tissue area of the section during pulling.
Bring an aluminum foil-covered 24-well cell culture plate within the hood of the cryotome.
Quickly transfer the cryo-section into one of the wells filled with 1× PBS using Graefe forceps.
Carefully touch the section onto the surface of 1× PBS.
The cryo-matrix will immediately dissolve in the buffer.
Critical: Keep the section away from the wall of the well.
Discard the 1× PBS containing dissolved PolyFreezeTM.
Add 500 μL 1× PBST to remove the cryo-matrix and start permeabilizing the thick tissue.
Repeat steps for obtaining cryo-sections for all immunolabeling experiments.
Observe sections under a stereo zoom microscope after obtaining requisite number of sections.
Transfer the 24-well cell culture plate, containing floating FL sections, on ice.
Place the plate on the 2D rocker at 15 rpm for 5 min.
Discard 1× PBST and perform biotin blocking for sections that require Streptavidin conjugated fluorophore addition.
Add 300 μL avidin to the sections.
Incubate at 24°C–26°C for 15 min.
Remove avidin and wash the sections with 300 μL 1× PBST for 5 min at 24°C–26°C.
Discard the wash buffer.
Add 300 μL biotin and incubate at 24°C–26°C for 15 min.
After 15 min, discard biotin and wash the sections for 5 min with 300 μL 1× PBST, at 24°C–26°C.
Prepare the optimal working concentration of primary antibody in 1× PBST.
Remove the wash buffer.
Add primary antibody to the sections.
Incubate for 2 h at 24°C–26°C or 16–24 h at 4°C, according to the conditions optimized for individual antibodies.
Wash sections with 1× PBST twice, for 5 min each, at 24°C–26°C after primary antibody incubation.
Prepare the working concentration for the secondary antibodies in 1× PBST.
Incubate the sections with the secondary antibody for 1–2.5 hours at 24°C–26°C.
Wash the sections with 1× PBST for 5 minutes at 24°C–26°C.
Repeat steps of preparing working concentration, incubating with secondary antibodies, and washing sections for all pairs of primary and secondary antibodies in the experimental combination.
Discard wash buffer and add 300 μL working concentration of Hoechst 33342 for 5–10 min at 24°C–26°C for counterstaining.
Perform Hoechst counterstaining only if secondary antibody in the excitation and emission range of Hoechst dye (AF405) is absent from the experiment combination.
Take a frosted slide and wipe it with lint-free tissue paper.
Lay the slide down on a black surface.
Use a PAP pen to draw circular hydrophobic boundaries on the frosted slide.
Allow the hydrophobic boundaries to completely dry before proceeding.
Add 100–200 μL of 1× PBS inside the boundary to create a convex aqueous surface.
Discard Hoechst and add 2 mL of 1× PBS into the sample well using a 200 μL tip.
Dip a wet, fine brush very carefully into the well and underneath the floating section without touching it.
Gently lift the brush out of the well such that the section layers the outer surface of the brush.
Hold the brush horizontally and gently roll the section off onto the aqueous convex surface built on the slides.
Use the pointed end of a folded lint-free tissue paper to remove the hydrophobic boundary surrounding the section.
Absorb leftover 1× PBS, taking care not to wipe off the tissue.
Add a drop of Prolong Gold anti-fade mountant slightly ahead of the section.
Place a coverslip on the drop of mounting media and let it spread across the edge before lowering it gently over the sample.
Make sure that the mounting media spreads uniformly over the entirety of the section after lowering the coverslip.
Remove bubbles with the help of a 200 μL tip if they are introduced.
Do not over-dry the sections before mounting them.
Carefully place the mounted slides in a dark area and leave them to dry at 24°C–26°C for approximately 16 hours.
Transfer the slides to 4°C after overnight drying until the samples are being imaged.
Place a drop of ImmersolTM 518F over the coverslip, covering the tissue section area.
Mount the slide on the slide holder of the microscope stage.
Use UV range light from the fluorescent lamp to coarsely focus the tissue section under 10× objective magnification.
Change the objective to Plan-Apochromat 63×/1.40 Oil DIC M27 lens and adjust fine focus knob until nucleus appears clear.
Move the stage in x-y plane to select a region of interest with proper vasculature.
Scan the area of interest through all channels.
Adjust laser intensity and gain master for optimal signal strength.
Denote the start and end z-steps of the total FL volume to be imaged.
Set the image size to 1024 × 1024 pixels.
Set the line average to 1.
Select unidirectional scan direction.
Choose PMT detector type.
Set pinhole to 1 Airy Unit.
Set z-increment (step-size) to 1 μm.
Set scan speed to 6 Hz.
Capture emission range for Ex633 nm from 636 nm to 758 nm.
Capture emission range for Ex561 nm from 561 nm to 635 nm.
Capture emission range for Ex488 nm from 492 nm to 560 nm.
Capture emission range for Ex405 nm from 408 nm to 487 nm.
Image 10-15 different areas on the tissue section.
Consider tile scanning to cover the entire area of the section.
Optionally, perform z-stack acquisition with tile scanning.
Name image files appropriately after imaging.
Save images in the designated folder.
Avoid imaging edges of the tissue to prevent non-specific fluorescence.
